title: Terraform module: redwood_private_eks_bootstrapper with upgrade-safety hooks and health probes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Author a reusable Terraform module 'redwood_private_eks_bootstrapper' to provision and harden Redwood Private EKS control-plane and core infra with built-in upgrade-safety hooks and health probes. The module should: (1) bootstrap EKS clusters in customer VPCs with opinionated defaults for S3/Dynamo state backends and cross-account KMS attachments; (2) provide safe upgrade primitives that can perform preflight validation, nodegroup rotation in a canary-first manner, and automated rollback triggers if health checks fail; (3) emit CloudWatch/Prometheus-friendly metrics and install (optional) observability sidecars for control-plane health; (4) include terratest suites and a CI pipeline for module validation; and (5) ship with a short runbook for on-call and rollout playbooks. Constraints: must be compatible with our existing terraform backend patterns, support cross-account KMS grants, and avoid any architecture that requires manual intervention for stateful upgrades. Non-goal: this ticket does not cover full private control plane UI or long-term autoscaler tuning (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Module package published under terraform-modules/redwood_private_eks_bootstrapper with semver tags
Module supports configuring S3 backend + DynamoDB state locking via inputs and documents the pattern
Preflight validator (redwood-eks-verify) runs as a null_resource/local-exec hook and fails early for common misconfigs
Upgrade hooks implement: canary nodegroup rotation -> smoke-health-checks -> either continue or trigger rollback flow
Health checks include: control-plane API latency threshold, kube-system critical pod readiness, kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager errors count
Terratest integration executed in CI that validates bootstrap, upgrade (minor version), and destroy paths on a sandbox account
Security review completed for KMS cross-account grant flow and IAM permissions documented
Runbook created and linked, including manual rollback commands and emergency contact list
implementation_notes: Module will expose inputs: cluster_name, eks_version, vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, node_groups (map), kms_key_arn_for_encryption, s3_backend_bucket, dynamodb_lock_table
Use aws_eks_addon and managed nodegroups where possible; for legacy unmanaged nodegroups provide lifecycle hooks for draining / cordon

Upgrade-safety pattern: terraform apply -> null_resource.preflight (exec redwood-eks-verify) -> plan for nodegroup rotation -> create temporary canary nodegroup with new AMI/launch template -> migrate small traffic (taints/labels) -> run health checks -> if pass, continue rotating remaining nodegroups in batches, else create rollback plan and notify

Health probes implemented as Lambda-backed custom resources that evaluate: pod readiness (kubelet metrics), apiserver latency (synthetic kubeclient queries), and kube-controller-manager errors. Results published to CloudWatch metrics namespace 'Redwood/EKS/Bootstrapper'
State backend: enforce Terraform S3 backend + DynamoDB lock via module docs; include helper script to bootstrap the bucket and lock table with correct encryption and kms grants
KMS: module accepts a kms_grant_principals list and writes a documented template for cross-account grants. Do not create global keys; reference existing keys when provided
Testing: terratest (Go) suite in infra-tests/eks_bootstrapper_test.go; CI job will run in sandbox account with env var gating. Use cost controls and auto-destroy on CI failure
Observability: optional install of 'redwood-eks-health-exporter' (helm chart) into kube-system if enable_health_exporter=true
Telemetery: emit module-level events to Datadog/CloudWatch via SNS for long-running operations (apply/upgrade/rollback)

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Terraform long-running operations may time out in CI -> Mitigation: break apply into smaller stages and surface a long-running job in Jenkins with extended timeout
Risk: Cross-account KMS grants might expose keys if misconfigured -> Mitigation: security review and automated IAM linting (tfsec, checkov) in CI
Risk: Canary nodegroup fails to emulate production traffic -> Mitigation: use synthetic traffic generator and label-based traffic steering for representative workloads
